posts.title: Use It Or Lose It: Winter Trips To Book Before Your PTO Disappears
posts.description: The end of the year just snuck up on us, didn’t it? And for a lot of us, so did the PTO we never got around to using. In fact, a 2025 survey reported by CNBC found that nearly a quarter of American workers hadn’t taken a single vacation day that year, and most of us only notice our unused PTO when it’s about to vanish. In the words of Iyanla Vanzant, “ not on my watch .” If your job has a use-it-or-lose-it policy, whatever you don’t use by December 31 is gone. Luckily, late December is when most of us can actually step away, so we rounded up seven trips that fit into those last few weeks. You’ll find Christmas markets, the Northern Lights, and a few beaches where your biggest decision is which pool to sit by. For each one, we’ve broken down how many days you need, what it costs, how to book on short notice and how Black travelers have been received there. posts.title: Estelle on Holiday Traditions, Kitchen Sisterhood, and Blending Jollof Rice With Thai Flavors
posts.description: When it comes to holiday eating, the best ingredient is a whole lot of friends. Just ask Estelle. The British-born singer embraces the holiday season, celebrating Christmas Eve right through the U.K.’s Boxing Day. After throwing a dinner party with her pal, Christy LoPresto, a New York City chef and restaurateur, where they blended their cultural flavors into the night’s meal, they knew they had to share it with the masses. The duo recently hosted a dinner party experience at LoPresto’s restaurant, Kin Thai, sharing their love of spices and sisterhood. The menu served up inventive fusions, like a jollof-and-Thai-fried-rice mix, and a spin on a Thai tea cake with a sponge cake base, hibiscus jam instead of strawberry jam, and banana vanilla cream. “It keeps strings of Thailand in there with the banana and the Thai cake, but also we made it West Indian again with the banana and the hibiscus jam,” Estelle shared.
